title: The Harbour Gazette
key_sentences: More than 900 people lined the quay on a bright September Saturday for the annual Lifeboat Day.
Together they raised £6,420, the largest sum in the event’s forty-year history.
From 5 October the passenger ferry will run a winter timetable with fewer sailings on weekends but an extra early crossing on weekdays.
Season tickets remain valid and can be renewed at the harbour office.
The association needs a new treasurer from January.
The winter issue will be delivered in the first week of December.

list_items.text: Weekdays: first sailing at 06.45, last at 21.15
Saturdays: first sailing at 08.30, last at 19.30
Sundays: first sailing at 10.00, last at 17.00

1. Plant bulbs at a depth of three times their height.
2. Choose a spot with good drainage and some sun.
3. Water once after planting and then leave them alone.
Poach 600 g of mixed white fish and smoked haddock in milk for ten minutes.
Make a white sauce with the strained milk, then fold in the flaked fish and a handful of parsley.
Cover with mashed potato and bake at 200 degrees for thirty minutes.

notes: Two-page community newsletter in Georgia with Palatino Linotype headings. The masthead is the title (level 1). Page 1 has THREE columns side by side; the reading order is column by column (left, middle, right), top to bottom. Column 2 holds a paragraph and a CSS-drawn bullet list (timetable); column 3 holds a "What's on" list with TYPED "• " markers (kept in item text) and a pull quote set in italics. Article headings are level 2, sub-heads level 3. Page 2 has two columns side by side (left: letters, a TYPED-number tip list "1." "2." "3." and harbour notes; right: classifieds table with a rule under the header only, then a recipe whose method is a CSS-drawn decimal list, no marker in text). The pull quote (italic, between two rules, column 2) is decorative and is not listed anywhere. The dateline under the masthead and the page footers are furniture; the page-1 footer is "Page one", the page-2 footer is "2 — The Harbour Gazette — Autumn 2026" (varied forms).
